It has recently been noted that malignant fibrous histio-cytoma is not associated with a distinct gene cluster, suggest-ing that malignant fibrous histiocytoma is not a separate tumor entity but rather a common morphologic appearance of various sarcoma subtypes.

For example, most tumors initially diag-nosed as malignant fibrous histiocytoma in the retroperitoneum have been reclassified using genomic profiling as dedifferenti-ated liposarcomas,56 whereas those in the extremities have been reclassified as leiomyosarcoma, myxofibrosarcoma, or pleo-morphic undifferentiated sarcoma.
